author: Mohsin Inamdar, open to work
text:
I've attended many interviews for AI and Generative AI roles over the past few months. Every time, I prepare, learn something new, and hope this will be the one.

Sometimes I wonder why I wasn't selected. Maybe another candidate had more experience, maybe there was an internal hire or a referral, or maybe I still have areas to improve. The truth is, I don't always know.

What I do know is that rejection is difficult, especially when you're working hard to upskill every day. But I'm choosing not to give up.

I'm continuing to build AI projects, improve my coding skills, strengthen my understanding of RAG, LangGraph, LLMs, and prepare for every interview with the hope that the right opportunity will come.

To everyone else who is searching for a job: you're not alone. Keep learning, keep applying, and keep believing in your journey. One opportunity can change everything.

If anyone is hiring for AI/ML, Generative AI, or Python Engineer roles, or has advice to share, I'd truly appreciate your support.

author: Grigoriy Dobryakov
text:
Job descriptions are more honest than keynotes. Keynotes say "AI is transforming everything." JDs name the specific layer that broke.

I went through a corpus of 2026 open roles — frontier lab, enterprise pharma, industrial Series C, an agent startup before Series A — and found five clusters that repeat. Not trends. Actual roles with measurable outcomes in the responsibilities section.

**1. Production agent ownership**

A VC-backed AI startup opening three Engineering Manager roles simultaneously, all for AI agents. Required track record: agents in production, evals, guardrails, HITL, orchestration. Target metric: automation from ~40% to 85–95%.

What this means: Customer Success can no longer carry delivery. The company is moving to engineering-led deployment before the round. The hiring structure is a proof point for investors.

**2. Applied AI leadership**

Sr. Director, Engineering — Applied AI: consolidates scattered AI initiatives into a managed delivery track. At AstraZeneca: Director, Enterprise AI Engineering — five zones from Systems Intelligence to Product Incubation, golden-path for AI development across a PhD-heavy team.

If your plan is "two strong ML engineers," these JDs are already describing a different org chart.

**3. Evals as infrastructure**

Anthropic is hiring a Prompt Engineer for Agent Prompts & Evals: eval frameworks, automated suites, regression testing on every model release across all product surfaces. The role's range: $320K–405K. An EM on the same line is opening in parallel.

Prompting is no longer a side task for an IC. It's becoming an infrastructure function with headcount. If you haven't assigned an owner — you're already behind frontier.

**4. Partner / field architecture**

Head of International Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships: a team of Partner Solutions Architects, GSI and cloud-partner coverage, reference architectures, enterprise production readiness.

Read as: the lab can't close enterprise deployments with internal capacity alone. Partner networks are already outpacing internal delivery — demand for implementation architects is real and growing.

**5. Industrial / domain autonomy**

CTO, UK remote, £150–190K + ~1.5–2% equity. In the mandate: "drive technical transition toward agentic AI and autonomous optimization." That's not a slide from the deck — it's what the role is for. Series C money is writing agentic transition into C-level job descriptions.

One vacancy is noise. Three overlapping roles at the same company is a drawing. Look at what broke, who is being hired next door, and where the success metric lives.

If the metric already says "production AI assets" and "evaluation harness" — that company is buying the discipline to run AI in production, not the enthusiasm to try it.

author: Abdullah Khan ⇌ AgilePreneur
text:
🚨 The career advice from 5 years ago is now actively hurting you.

"Learn to code."
"Get a degree."
"Climb the corporate ladder."

Cute advice. For 2019.

It's 2026. AI didn't just change the tools we use — it changed which *jobs exist at all.*

Here's the uncomfortable truth nobody's saying out loud on LinkedIn:

You don't need to become an AI engineer to survive this shift.
You need to become someone who knows how to work WITH AI, better than the person next to you.

That's it. That's the whole game right now.

I've spent the last few weeks going deep on what's actually hiring in the AI economy — not the hype, not the "prompt engineer will make you rich" nonsense — the real roles companies are filling today.

Here's the genuine list:

𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗸
• AI/ML Engineer
• AI Integration Specialist (bolting AI into existing products)
• MLOps Engineer
• AI Data Engineer
• Agentic AI / Workflow Developer

𝗡𝗼𝗻𝗰𝗼𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗯𝘂𝘁 𝗔𝗜𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗸 (this is where most people should start)
• AI Response Evaluator / Model Grader
• Data Annotator / Labeler
• Prompt Writer & Prompt QA Specialist
• Domain Expert Reviewer (legal, medical, finance, engineering backgrounds especially in demand)
• AI Safety / Policy Reviewer
• Language Specialist (native speakers evaluating model output in non English languages)
• AI Agent Workflow Tester

𝗕𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀 & 𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝘆 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗸
• AI Product Manager
• AI Implementation Consultant
• AI Content Strategist
• Automation/Ops Specialist (identifying what to automate)

Notice something? Most of these don't require a CS degree. They require judgment, domain expertise, and the willingness to actually learn the tools instead of complaining about them.

𝗪𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗼 𝗮𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗹𝗼𝗼𝗸 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗻𝗼𝘄 (live, remote friendly boards, not random links):
→ LinkedIn Jobs — filter "Remote" + "AI"
→ ZipRecruiter's remote AI listings (updated daily)
→ Remote work boards specializing in AI evaluator/annotator roles (Mercor, Outlier, micro1, Handshake AI all actively hiring for eval/annotation work, no coding required)

author: Tarana Matloob
text:
Founders usually ask a recruiter one question first: "How fast can you fill this?"

I've started leading with a different one: "Here's exactly where this person falls short — still want to talk to them?"

A recent example: a backend engineer with strong distributed-systems chops, but his GenAI experience was mostly exploratory, not production. I told the client that upfront, before he asked, instead of letting him find out three interviews in.

He still took the call — decided the fundamentals mattered more than the AI gap for this particular role, and made an offer two weeks later.

That's the actual value of the honest-flag approach: it doesn't lower your close rate, it raises your close confidence. Founders make faster, better decisions when they're not managing a recruiter's sales pitch on top of a hiring decision.

I work with early-stage AI/ML, data, and backend teams on exactly this. If you're hiring right now, happy to send a profile over with the gaps included — no polish, no pitch.

author: Mikkel Nielsen
text:
Which engineering job is growing fastest in European tech?

Most people would say AI Engineer. When I actually checked our data, it wasn't.

Hiring is up across the board, so I measured each title against that overall growth, to find the one that genuinely pulled ahead of the field. It was the Forward Deployed Engineer, the engineer who sits inside the customer until the software works.

Ranked by how much each outgrew engineering hiring overall:
1️⃣ Forward Deployed Engineer
2️⃣ Security Engineer 
3️⃣ Software Engineer 
4️⃣ AI / ML Engineer 
5️⃣ Data Engineer

The role everyone assumes is the rocket isn't the one moving fastest.

I unpacked the whole shift in this month's edition of The Benchmark, our new monthly read of the European hiring market.

text:
Zero downtime. That's the part people skip when they talk about cloud migrations.

Before I built visa trackers and HVAC calculators, I spent 5+ years as a BI and Data Engineer. One of the harder stretches: migrating a live production data pipeline to Snowflake and SQL Server for enterprise clients across the US, UK, and Canada, without a single outage window anyone noticed.

No maintenance banner. No "service degraded" message. No 2am rollback.

That work earned Datafortune's High Five Award in 2023. But the number I'm actually proud of is smaller and far less dramatic: we automated ETL and SSRS workflows that cut manual reporting effort by 60%, while holding 100% SLA compliance the entire time. Nobody claps for SLA compliance. It's the metric that just has to stay boring.

I moved into AI and mobile product building after that. The instinct carried over: ship the thing, keep it running, don't let the people depending on it notice the seams.

If you're hiring for Data Engineering, BI, or AI/ML roles and want someone who's already done the unglamorous version of "reliable" at enterprise scale, that's also me.

text:
Just wrapped up learning the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and created a simple architecture diagram to better understand how everything connects.

One thing I really liked about MCP is that it provides a standard way for AI applications to interact with external tools and data sources without building custom integrations every time.

A few key concepts I explored:
• MCP Client – Sends requests from AI applications or agents.
• MCP Protocol – Handles communication using STDIO (for local servers) or HTTP (for remote servers).
• MCP Server – Exposes tools, resources, and prompts that AI models can use.

This helped me understand how AI agents can securely connect to databases, APIs, files, and other services through a common interface.
I'm currently diving deeper into Agentic AI, MCP, LangGraph, RAG, and AI application development, and it's been exciting to see how these technologies fit together.

author: Andy MacKay
text:
The programming skills companies actually need right now

Lat week I had three different hiring managers ask for the same thing “someone who knows Go and understands distributed systems”

That’s not a coincidence

Here’s what’s happening in the Norwegian market
Companies aren’t asking for Swiss Army knife developers anymore. They’re asking for specialists with strong fundamentals

What’s in high demand
Python- the workhorse. Data engineering, backends, AI/ML still the safe bet
Go- systems that need to scale. Performance + readability. Fintech loves it
TypeScript- full-stack teams building modern products, not negotiable anymore
Kotlin- enterprise modernisation. Java shops upgrading their code
Rust- the prestige language. Systems programming, blockchain, performance critical work

What’s not as hot
Ruby, PHP still used but demand is shrinking. JavaScript it’s moving backwards without Typescript

The real insight
Companies care less about the language, more about what you can build with it
Can you design systems? Can you think about concurrency? Can you optimise for production? Can you write code that other people want to maintain?

Those skills transcend language

If you’re early in your career
Pick Python or Go, learn deeply, understand architecture. The specific language matters less than the thinking

If you’re established
Your second language should be very different from your first. If you know Python, learn Go or Rust. If you know JavaScript, learn Kotlin or Clouje. Forces you to think differently

The market reality
There aren’t enough Go developers in Norway. There aren’t enough Rust engineers. There are plenty of Python developers but good ones are hard to find

What language are you learning or mastering right now?

author: Muhammad Ali
text:
A few months ago, someone asked me a simple question.

"Which AI should my business use?"

It sounded like a straightforward question.

It wasn't.

Because asking that is like walking into a hospital and asking,

"Which doctor do I need?"

Well...

What's the problem?

AI works the same way.

There isn't one AI.

There are different types.

And each one has a different job.

Here's the simplest way to think about them:

📋 Rules-Based AI follows instructions.
Like a checklist that never forgets.

📊 Machine Learning learns from past data.
Like an analyst spotting patterns you can't easily see.

🧠 Deep Learning understands complex information.
Think speech, language, and recommendations.

👁️ Computer Vision gives AI eyes.
It reads documents, detects defects, and verifies identities.

✍️ Generative AI creates.
Emails.
Reports.
Code.
Images.
Presentations.

🤖 AI Agents take action.
They don't just answer questions.
They complete work.

🌍 World Models are what's coming next.
AI that can understand environments, predict outcomes, and plan before acting.

Here's what I've learned.

Most AI projects don't fail because the model is bad.

They fail because the business picks the wrong type of AI for the job.

That's like hiring a brilliant designer to do your accounting.

The talent isn't the problem.

The fit is.

Before asking,

"Which AI tool should we buy?"

Ask a better question.

"What job are we trying to get done?"

That answer usually points you to the right type of AI long before it points you to the right vendor.

Which type of AI is creating the most value in your organization today? 👇

♻️ Repost this to help someone understand how modern AI systems actually work.

Follow Muhammad Ali for practical insights on AI automation, cybersecurity, agentic AI, and turning technology into measurable business outcomes.

author: Taye Oladugba
text:
The Psychological Impact of Unemployment on Job Seekers 💡 

Being unemployed is more than not having a job.

For many job seekers, it can affect confidence, self-esteem, motivation, relationships, and even how they see themselves. The constant applications, interviews, assessments, and rejection emails can gradually create thoughts like:

"Maybe I'm not good enough."
"Maybe my experience doesn't matter."
"Maybe I'll never get another opportunity."

But please remember this: Your current employment status is not a measure of your worth or your ability.

A rejection does not mean you are incapable.
A delayed opportunity does not mean you have been forgotten.
Not getting the job today does not mean you won't get it tomorrow.

Job searching can be emotionally exhausting, but don't allow the process to convince you that you have nothing to offer.

Keep improving your CV.
Keep learning.
Keep applying.
Keep networking.
Keep showing up.

And most importantly, give yourself permission to rest without feeling guilty. You are human, not a machine.

To every job seeker currently wondering when their "Yes" will come: Don't stop trying. Your next opportunity could come from an application you almost didn't submit, a connection you almost didn't make, or a conversation you almost didn't have.

Keep going. Your story is still being written.

And to recruiters and hiring managers: Remember that there is a human being behind every application. A little communication, feedback, or encouragement can make a significant difference to someone going through a difficult season.

👉🏿 To every job seeker out there—your season will change. Keep going. 🤝

🚦 Think AI in cities is just a futuristic sci-fi concept? Think again.
Cities aren't waiting for the future—they are deploying AI right now to fix traffic, speed up transit, and make streets safer. And the best part? They aren't even hiring armies of $2M machine learning engineers to do it.

🚑 Edge AI is rewriting the rules. Instead of sending massive video feeds to the cloud, modern traffic lights process data right at the intersection. If an ambulance approaches, the local camera hears the siren, recognizes the vehicle, and clears the lane instantly. (smartcitiesworld.net)

author: Anadia Shabira Vasya
text:
Lapangan Kerja Baru yang Lahir dari Adopsi AI, apa saja itu?

Perubahan di dunia kerja adalah sesuatu yang tidak bisa dihindari. Kehadiran Generative AI sempat memunculkan kekhawatiran bahwa banyak profesi akan tergantikan oleh mesin.
Namun, yang terjadi saat ini justru menunjukkan arah yang berbeda.
Alih-alih hanya menghilangkan pekerjaan, AI juga menciptakan berbagai peran baru yang sebelumnya belum pernah ada. Perusahaan kini tidak hanya mencari talenta yang mampu coding atau mendesain secara manual, tetapi juga individu yang mampu memanfaatkan AI untuk meningkatkan produktivitas sekaligus memberikan dampak nyata bagi bisnis.

Beberapa profesi yang permintaannya mulai meningkat antara lain:
🔹 Prompt Engineer
Profesional yang bertugas menyusun instruksi (prompt), struktur bahasa, dan alur logika agar sistem AI seperti Large Language Models (LLMs) mampu menghasilkan output yang akurat, relevan, minim bias, serta aman digunakan dalam operasional perusahaan.
🔹 AI Product / Project Manager
Profesional yang bertanggung jawab mengintegrasikan teknologi AI ke dalam proses bisnis. Perannya mencakup menyusun strategi implementasi, memastikan tata kelola data dan etika penggunaan AI, hingga mengukur dampak bisnis serta Return on Investment (ROI) dari implementasi teknologi tersebut.

Apa Kata Data?
📊 World Economic Forum (WEF) melalui Future of Jobs Report memprediksi bahwa kebutuhan terhadap spesialis AI dan Machine Learning akan meningkat sekitar 40%, setara dengan terciptanya sekitar 1 juta lapangan kerja baru secara global. Hal ini menunjukkan bahwa transformasi berbasis AI justru membuka peluang kolaborasi yang lebih besar antara manusia dan teknologi.

📈 McKinsey Technology Trends Outlook 2025 juga menunjukkan bahwa investasi perusahaan terhadap Generative AI meningkat secara signifikan. Banyak organisasi bahkan bersedia memberikan kompensasi di atas rata-rata pasar untuk mendapatkan talenta yang mampu memimpin implementasi sistem AI, termasuk pengembangan Agentic AI.
Bagaimana HR dan Profesional Tech Harus Bersiap?
Bagi praktisi HR, perkembangan ini menghadirkan tantangan baru dalam menyusun job description, menentukan kompetensi, hingga merancang indikator penilaian untuk peran-peran yang bahkan belum memiliki standar baku.
Karena itu, pendekatan Skills-Based Hiring menjadi semakin relevan. Fokus penilaian tidak lagi hanya pada latar belakang pendidikan atau jurusan, tetapi pada kemampuan kandidat untuk terus belajar, beradaptasi dengan teknologi baru, serta memanfaatkan AI secara efektif dalam menyelesaikan permasalahan bisnis🧐. 
Di sisi lain, bagi para profesional teknologi, kemampuan teknis saja mungkin tidak lagi cukup. Memahami kebutuhan bisnis, mampu berkolaborasi lintas fungsi, dan mengetahui bagaimana AI dapat menciptakan nilai tambah akan menjadi kompetensi yang semakin dibutuhkan di masa depan.

Source:

• McKinsey – Technology Trends Outlook 2025

author: Unknown Author
text:
The New Interview Question Is “Why?”

The answer is no longer the strongest hiring signal. The reasoning behind it is.

Imagine asking a product candidate:
“A new feature increased user growth, but the paid conversion rate declined. What would you investigate?”
They immediately propose channel segmentation, funnel analysis, cohort comparisons and A/B testing.
It sounds correct.
Then comes the real question:
“Why would you start with acquisition channels rather than product usage?”
That follow-up is becoming more important because AI can now generate polished frameworks, reports, code and take-home assignments in minutes.

Greenhouse reported that 39% of US hiring managers were conducting more in-person interviews to verify candidate authenticity. Companies are responding in two apparently opposite ways:
McKinsey prohibits generative AI, external websites and prepared notes in specified assessments and interviews. In contrast, Canva expects candidates for selected backend, frontend and machine-learning roles to use tools such as Copilot, Cursor and Claude during technical interviews. These approaches are not truly contradictory.

They test two sides of the same capability:
- Can you reason independently without AI?
- Can you retain judgment while working with AI?
- Can you identify unsupported assumptions?
- Can you verify outputs rather than accept them?
- Can you explain why one option fits the constraints better than another?

AI fluency is not simply prompt fluency.
It is the ability to define the problem, provide the right context, evaluate alternatives, challenge the model and remain accountable for the result.
As outputs become easier to generate, interviews will increasingly test what remains difficult to automate:
judgment, verification, adaptation and responsibility.
How is your organisation redesigning interviews for AI-assisted work?

author: Manon Claus’ profile
text:
DYNAMIC PAYCHECKS..
*welkom in de consequenties van uw 'ik heb niets te verbergen'-toekomst*

We zijn al bekend met 'dynamic pricing': de prijs van een product verandert per klant of minuut, afhankelijk van algoritmes die in de gaten houden hoe gewild een product is, hoeveel het bij de concurrent kost, hoeveel er nog op voorraad is en nog veel meer 'neutrale' variabelen.
Maar ook op basis van jouw eigen gedrag: 'Machine learning programs analyze user behavior, to set optimal price points.'

Het klinkt heel onschuldig met termen als 'flexibel' en 'optimal', maar het doel is natuurlijk niet om jou de beste prijs te bieden, maar om je over te halen tot een aankoop. Dus om jou geld te laten uitgeven.

De algoritmes werken daarvoor met álle data die ze over je kunnen verzamelen, dus ook jouw postcode, welke browser je gebruikt, hoevaak je een product hebt gekocht, hoe loyaal je aan bepaalde merken bent, of je gevoelig bent voor korting, kortom: alles wat ze kunnen vinden. En dat wordt (met behulp van AI datacenters) steeds meer.

Guess what: dit principe wordt nu ook al toegepast (alhoewel doorgaans ontkent) in salariëring. 

'Experts describe “surveillance wages” as a system in which wages are based not on an employee’s performance or seniority, but on formulas that use their personal data, often collected without employees’ knowledge.

Dat begint al vóórdat je wordt aangenomen. 
Het algoritme zoekt online naar info over:

Financiele stabiliteit: heb je leningen, creditcards? Oftewel: hoezeer heb je deze baan nodig, want dan accepteer je waarschijnlijk een lager aanbod.

Sociale Media: hoe activistisch ben je, zou je je bij een vakbond aansluiten? Wat is de kans dat je een gezin wilt stichten, aka binnenkort zwanger zult zijn?

'Surveillance wages don’t stop at the hiring stage, they follow workers onto the job, too. These programs offer tools that are built to set bonus or incentive compensation, track productivity, customer interactions and real-time behavior, including, in some cases, audio and video surveillance on the job.

Nearly 70% of companies with more than 500 employees were already using employee-monitoring systems in 2022.

The system makes assumptions about how big of an incentive they need to give to a particular worker to generate the behavioral response they seek.

The platforms adjust pay, based on what they know, including how often f.i. a nurse accepts shifts, how quickly they respond to postings and what pay they have accepted in the past. Uber rolled out new pay algorithms years ago,  drivers were offered different base fares for the same trip. They were shown a take-it-or-leave-it rate, which rises only after enough drivers reject it.

Forget about the gender pay gap..
Iedereen wordt elkaars concurrent & the race to the bottom..

text:
Most people will focus on the robot. 🤖

The more important story is what sits behind it.

Google DeepMind’s Gemini Robotics 2 shows how quickly the gap between AI reasoning and physical action is beginning to close. A humanoid robot that can walk, crouch, manipulate objects and complete multi-step tasks is impressive, but the real development is the model’s ability to understand its environment, plan ahead and coordinate its whole body through one connected system.

For years, AI has performed best in digital environments, while robotics has relied on separate systems for perception, movement and decision-making. Gemini Robotics 2 points towards a future where those capabilities are brought together.

That changes the conversation for employers.

The key question is no longer whether robots will become more capable. It is how organisations will redesign work when AI can reason, respond and act in the physical world. 🧠

That will create demand for people who can work across robotics, machine learning, computer vision and physical AI, while also understanding how these systems fit into real operating environments.

The organisations preparing their workforce and talent strategy now will be better placed to turn embodied intelligence into practical value.

author: Hamsa Medhat, open to work
text:
I'm excited to share that I have achieved an A+ on my Bachelor's Thesis at the German University in Cairo! 🎉
Over the past several months, I developed an Explainable Resume Matching System Using Natural Language Processing (NLP), designed to make AI-powered recruitment more accurate, transparent, and trustworthy.
The system follows a two-phase pipeline. First, it parses resumes and job descriptions, performs exact and semantic skill matching using a fine-tuned E5 embedding model, and applies a LightGBM classifier to determine whether a candidate is qualified for the role. Qualified candidates then move to the second phase, where they are ranked using configurable weighted criteria such as skills, experience, education, certifications, and an optional cross-encoder reranker. Finally, the system generates human-readable explanations for every decision using a Large Language Model, allowing recruiters to understand why a candidate was selected or rejected instead of relying on a black-box prediction.
In addition to intelligent resume matching and ranking, the system includes:
1-Resume and job description parsing.
2-Explainable AI for transparent hiring decisions.
3-Comparative candidate analysis.
4-Automated interview scheduling through Google Calendar integration and email notifications.
5-A recruiter-friendly web application that streamlines the recruitment process.

I'm proud that the proposed system achieved 96.00% accuracy, 92.86% precision, 92.86% recall, and a 92.86% F1-score, outperforming several state-of-the-art approaches while addressing one of the biggest challenges in AI recruitment systems: explainability.
This project has been an incredible learning journey that strengthened my knowledge in Artificial Intelligence, Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning, Explainable AI, Information Retrieval, and full-stack software development. More importantly, it taught me how to transform research into a practical system that solves a real-world problem.
I would like to express my sincere gratitude to Associate Professor
Milad Ghantous, PhD for his continuous guidance, invaluable feedback, and unwavering support throughout the implementation of this project. Your mentorship played a significant role in helping me achieve the best possible outcome.
Finally, I would like to thank my family, friends, and everyone who supported and encouraged me throughout this journey.
I'm excited for what comes next and look forward to building AI systems that create real impact.

author: Unknown Author
text:
The biggest forecasting problem in European SMEs isn't the wrong model — it's no model at all.

Most small and mid-sized businesses still rely on manual projections built from last quarter's numbers and intuition. That approach breaks the moment demand shifts, a supplier delays, or a seasonal pattern deviates. Time series forecasting exists to replace that fragility with structure.

The landscape of available methods has expanded dramatically. Classical statistical approaches like ARIMA handle stable, linear patterns well. But real business data — with its irregular seasonality, external shocks, and compounding variables — increasingly demands machine learning and AI-driven models that adapt to complexity without hand-tuned parameters.

Here's what gets overlooked: the sophistication of the model matters far less than the quality of the data pipeline feeding it. Inconsistent historical records, missing data points, and poorly defined variables will sabotage any forecast, no matter how advanced the algorithm. Data readiness is the actual bottleneck.

SMEs that treat forecasting as core operational infrastructure — not a finance-team side project — make faster, sharper decisions on inventory, cash flow, and hiring.

5 minutes into the interview, I realized my candidate wasn't human.

A recruiter described talking to a "candidate" who spoke for two minutes straight, perfectly fluent, no breath, no filler, no stumbles. 

She asked the same question three times. Identical answer three times. 

Then the call dropped. She'd spent 40 minutes interviewing an AI. 

HR later found the real person joined for the first 30 seconds… then let the bot take over. 

This isn't a fringe case. Insiders estimate 15–20% of video interviews at high-volume teams now involve a bot or a paid proxy. 

Your ATS has exactly zero defense against this.

Has this happened to you yet, a candidate you're *pretty sure* wasn't real?

author: Dave Kline
text:
Great managers aren't more talented than you.

They're running a system you haven't built yet.

After working with thousands of leaders, 
I'm convinced management isn't a gift.
It's a set of learnable skills.

And those skills combine into a system.  

Here's the blueprint for you to copy:

1. Self-Awareness (the foundation)
↳ Know your mindset, abilities, and blind spots.
↳ Supplement your struggles, amplify your advantages.
↳ Write your personal operating manual so your team can work with you.

2. Clear Expectations (alignment)
↳ Co-author them with your team. Don't dictate.
↳ Define both the what and the how.
↳ Document what "exceeding" looks like, and recalibrate quarterly.

3. Thoughtful Delegation (leverage)
↳ Transfer ownership, not just tasks.
↳ Match the right work to the right person.
↳ Resist the urge to rescue the moment it gets hard.

4. Deliberate Development (growth)
↳ Coach strengths over weaknesses. Roughly 70/30.
↳ Give everyone a simple 3-bullet growth plan.
↳ Deliver feedback the same day you see it.

5. Systems (reliability)
↳ Run the minimum viable cadence of meetings.
↳ Build dashboards that surface the metrics that matter.
↳ Design processes that make success the default.

6. Diagnosing Problems (compounding)
↳ Find the real bottleneck, not the loudest symptom.
↳ Ask "why" five times to reach the root cause.
↳ Fix the system, not just the person.

7. Relentless Recruiting (talent)
↳ Build your pipeline before you need it.
↳ Test capability with work samples, not just interviews.
↳ Hire for character, not just credentials.

Here's the part that matters.

None of this is exotic. 
None of it requires permission.

You could start today.

But most managers won't. 
They'll keep relying on instinct and hope.

The ones who build the system don't get lucky.
They become leaders worth following.

author: Unknown Author
text:
Sanofi expanded its Toronto AI centre of excellence with a $294M commitment in May, scaling a 150-plus person team focused on drug discovery, manufacturing, and commercial operations. In the same month, Merck Group's $1B Google Cloud deal and Novo Nordisk's OpenAI partnership were both active.
 
Put the three together and the build vs buy question in pharma AI has become a strategic decision, not an operational one.
 
The case for Sanofi's model: proprietary infrastructure means the models, the data, and the compounding advantage stay inside the organisation. No vendor dependency. No partnership that can be renegotiated. The capability built for one function can be extended to another without a commercial conversation.
 
The case against: the cost is real, the talent competition is intense (you are recruiting against the AI companies whose tools you are trying to replicate), and the model runway may lag behind what a frontier AI company can deploy on a rolling basis.
 
For commercial teams at mid-size pharma companies not in a position to make $294M infrastructure bets, the practical version of this question is more tractable: which specific workflows in your commercial operations require you to own the AI layer, and which can safely run on a vendor's infrastructure without creating data, IP, or competitive risk?
 
That framing, own vs license by workflow, not by budget, is where the decision actually lives for most teams.
 
Which part of your commercial AI would you not want running on someone else's infrastructure?

text:
Everyone is talking about replacing jobs with AI.
I think they’re asking the wrong question.

The real question is:
Which workflows exist only because software wasn’t capable enough five years ago?

We just published a case study showing how we used Perplexity, AI agents, and workflow automation to engineer an end-to-end recruiting system.
Not to make recruiters more productive.

To eliminate the need for much of the recruiting workflow altogether.
For decades, recruiting firms have been paid to perform work that software simply couldn’t.

Finding candidates.
Researching backgrounds.
Personalizing outreach.
Following up.
Scheduling interviews.
Moving information from one system to another.

Today, that work can be engineered.
That’s not a criticism of recruiters.
It’s an observation about technology.

Every major technology shift removes intermediary layers.
Travel agents.
Stock brokers.
Video rental stores.
Recruiting is next.

The companies that understand this won’t build larger recruiting organizations.
They’ll build better hiring systems.

Perplexity is one of the technologies making this possible.

Our job at FullFunnel is figuring out how to combine tools like Perplexity with AI agents, automation, and operational design to fundamentally change how companies build revenue teams.

This is what applied AI actually looks like.

author: Randy Carr
text:
Every CEO I know is hiring to grow. This week I banned a whole category of hiring.

The rule, set on this week's AI build call: if an agent will likely do the job within 12 to 24 months, we do not hire the human first. We build the agent, then hire the people to support it. Never the reverse.

This is not a hiring freeze. We are recruiting an AI automation engineer right now. Marketing is adding a completely different talent stack. Sales is next. It is a sequencing rule.

Here is the math behind it. A hire into a role automation is about to swallow costs two years of salary, plus the worst part: I would have to unwind a person, not a project. People deserve better than being hired into a dead end I could already see.

I told the team building the system with me: congratulations, you now have our hiring thesis too.

And yes, the rule has to apply to the org chart that already exists. Including my seat. Mine has a date on it: December 31, 2028.

Look at your open requisitions. Which one are you filling because it is how you solved this problem in 2019?

author: Unknown Author
text:
Why is sourcing human data still one of the biggest bottlenecks in enterprise AI?

Because collecting human data isn't the hard part. Collecting enterprise-ready human data is.

Every AI team we speak with eventually encounters the same four challenges:
+ High Cost – Recruiting and managing participants at scale is expensive.
+ Low Quality – Generic datasets often lack the specificity needed for real-world AI applications.
+ Unclear Ownership – Third-party data can leave unanswered questions around provenance, usage rights and commercial ownership.
+ Lack of Compliance – Without explicit consent and proper documentation, legal and regulatory risk increases significantly.

These challenges become even more important as AI moves from experimentation into production.

Building AI isn't just about acquiring more human data.

It's about acquiring the right human data - with the quality, rights, provenance and governance enterprises need to deploy with confidence.

That's why we believe trusted human data is becoming foundational infrastructure for enterprise AI.

author: Freddie (Faham) Nazir
text:
Nobody talks about the real cost of a bad offshore hire.

It's not the salary. It's 3 months of onboarding, cratered sprint velocity, and a senior engineer burning 10 hours a week reviewing code that should never have shipped.

I've seen US teams lose $40,000+ on one wrong hire before they even knew it was wrong.

So before signing with any offshore or AI engineering provider, interrogate one thing: the quality guarantee.

Most fail this test.

Here's what a real one looks like:

Replacement, not refund. A refund leaves the seat empty. A replacement means a new vetted engineer in days, not another 8-week search.

No lock-in. If they need a 6-month contract to keep you, the contract IS the guarantee. Two weeks' notice means they earn the seat every month.

Vetting you can see. Live coding, system design, English fluency, and daily fluency with Cursor, Claude, Copilot. An engineer without AI leverage is running 2023 speed on your 2026 roadmap.

No recruiting fee. A $15-20K placement fee is a hostage situation. You'll tolerate mediocrity because replacing them costs another fee.

The uncomfortable truth: most providers optimize for placement volume, not placement survival. Their incentive dies the day yours begins.

At Divogue, roughly 3 in 100 engineers pass vetting. Sounds like a flex. It's just math, a guarantee only works if the funnel is brutal.

Ask any provider: "What happens on day 20 when the hire isn't working?"
Their answer tells you everything.

author: Kiara Obeyesekere
text:
The most important AI team at Meta has only 50–100 people.

That single number completely changed how I think about scaling technical teams.

Mark Zuckerberg's philosophy for building Meta's super intelligence team goes against how most companies scale.

Most organizations believe bigger teams create better outcomes.

His argument is almost the opposite.

AI research is a high-bandwidth problem.

If everyone can't keep the entire project in their head, execution slows down.

Every additional layer adds communication overhead. 

Every weak hire reduces the effectiveness of everyone around them.

That's why Meta is optimizing for talent density over headcount.

- A small team of exceptional researchers.
- A flat organization with minimal management.
- No arbitrary deadlines for research.
- Founders personally recruiting the best people.

This isn't just an AI strategy.

It's a reminder that some of the highest-leverage work comes from small groups of extraordinary people, not massive organizations.

The question isn't "How fast can we hire?"

It's "Who deserves a seat on the boat?"




Video credits: Mark Zuckerberg via Rowan Cheung podcast.

author: Kalyani Ghule
text:
Microsoft documented a hiring threat that begins with a normal Workday job application.


Not a compromised employee account.
Not a phishing link.
An applicant.

Microsoft’s April research described a North Korea-aligned actor mapping external career sites, calling Workday hrrecruiting/* endpoints, submitting tailored applications under fabricated identities and after a successful hire using the new Workday profile to set up payroll details from known hostile infrastructure.

That makes Workday Recruiting an identity-security surface as well as a talent-acquisition surface.

Workday 2026R1 has given teams candidate signals such as:
-Automation Score.
-Application duration.
-Requisition count.
-Geolocation.
-IP address, ASN and JA4 fingerprint.

These can help a team notice a pattern.

They cannot tell a team that a person is fraudulent.

Microsoft explicitly says the same Recruiting API activity can be legitimate. 

Its documented distinction was repeated behaviour across accounts, infrastructure, interview communication and later sign-in activity.

So an Automation Score should open a case.
It should not close a career.

Between a score and an employment decision, I would want five controls:
1. REVIEW TRIGGER
->Define the combination that earns a review: a candidate signal plus a repeating API/account pattern, threat-intelligence match, or credible identity/interview inconsistency.

->Never one score alone.

2. DATA BOUNDARY
->Review who can see Candidate Data: Job Application and raw IP, location and fingerprint data.

->Privacy and Legal should define jurisdiction-specific purpose, notice, retention and need-to-know access before broad enablement.

3. ADJUDICATION PATH
->Recruiting, Security and the relevant HR/privacy owner need one shared escalation path to distinguish legitimate automation from fraud.

->A recruiter should not have to read the score and guess.

4. EVIDENCE TRAIL
-> Record what triggered the review, corroborating and counter-evidence, decision owner, disposition and false-positive resolution.

A defensible process needs more than a screenshot.

5.POST-HIRE HANDOFF
->The risk does not disappear at Hire.

->Microsoft observed suspicious payroll changes, anonymous-proxy activity, impossible travel and unusual search/download behaviour in connected apps after onboarding.

Your new-hire security monitoring needs to know which exceptions deserve a closer look.

Workday says its AI is designed to inform hiring teams, not automatically hire or reject candidates.

Candidate signals deserve the same discipline.

A signal can open a case.

Only evidence, context and accountable human judgement should close it.

This is the kind of Workday Security judgement we teach in our Live Workday HCM Course.

author: Prof. Dr. Andreas Moring
text:
Die größte Gefahr der KI ist nicht, dass sie Menschen ersetzt. Sondern dass Unternehmen vergessen, welche Menschen sie jetzt brauchen.
Während Führungsetagen nach KI-Kompetenz, Zertifikaten und neuen Tools suchen, sehen Talent-Verantwortliche einen ganz anderen Engpass:
73 Prozent nennen kritisches Denken und Problemlösung als wichtigste Recruiting-Priorität. KI-Skills landen nur auf Platz fünf!!
Das ist kein Widerspruch.
Denn KI kann Informationen verarbeiten, Muster erkennen und Ergebnisse produzieren. Aber sie kann uns die Verantwortung für diese Ergebnisse nicht abnehmen. Menschen müssen erkennen, wenn eine Antwort plausibel klingt, aber falsch ist.
Sie müssen Widersprüche sehen, Zusammenhänge verstehen und entscheiden, wann ein KI-Ergebnis genutzt, hinterfragt oder verworfen werden sollte. Und sie müssen künftig Teams führen, in denen Menschen und KI-Agenten Seite an Seite arbeiten. Der Erfolg von Unternehmen wird deshalb nicht allein davon abhängen, welche KI sie einsetzen. Er wird davon abhängen, wie gut ihre Mitarbeiter denken, urteilen, lernen, kommunizieren und entscheiden.
Technologie lässt sich einkaufen. Menschliche Urteilskraft nicht so einfach bestellen und anschalten. Sie entsteht durch Erfahrung, Reflexion und Training.
Deshalb müssen wir kritisches Denken, Intuition, Anpassungsfähigkeit und Verantwortungsbewusstsein endlich als das behandeln, was sie sind: Entscheidende Zukunftskompetenzen.
Denn je leistungsfähiger die Maschinen werden, desto bewusster müssen wir das trainieren, was uns als Menschen stark macht. Dafür ist TheEssence da. Wir trainieren die zehn "AI-Future-Skills" mit klarer Diagnostik, Methodik und praktischen Übungen individuell und für Teams.

author: Mahesh Singh
text:
Period	Major Shift	Scarce Skill	Biggest Opportunity

1945–1965	Rebuilding after WWII	Physical labor, manufacturing	Stable factory and government jobs
1965–1985	Industrial expansion	Education, engineering	Middle-class careers
1985–2005	Computer revolution	Computer literacy	Software, finance, telecom
2005–2020	Internet & smartphones	Building online businesses, software	Apps, e-commerce, startups
2020–2025	Creator economy	Attention and content	YouTube, Instagram, influencers
2025 onward	AI revolution	Using AI to multiply productivity	AI-enabled professionals and businesses


The pattern repeats every 20–30 years

Every major technological shift follows a similar cycle:

1. A new technology appears.
2. People think it will destroy jobs.
3. Some jobs disappear.
4. New jobs emerge that didn't exist before.
5. Those who adapt early benefit the most.

Examples:

The Industrial Revolution reduced many artisan jobs but created factories, railways, and engineering.

Electricity replaced many manual systems but created electrical engineering and modern manufacturing.

Computers replaced typists but created software developers, IT, cybersecurity, and data science.

The Internet hurt newspapers but created digital marketing, e-commerce, cloud computing, and app development.


Today, AI is following the same pattern.

Why AI feels different

Unlike previous technologies, AI doesn't just replace physical work.

It can also perform parts of knowledge work:

writing,

coding,

designing,

analyzing,

customer support.


That makes white-collar professionals feel the same uncertainty factory workers felt decades ago.

But AI still has limits. It needs people to:

define problems,

make decisions,

verify outputs,

communicate with clients,

integrate systems,

take responsibility.


What usually survives every revolution

Across history, people who combine technical ability with human skills tend to do well.

These include:

solving real business problems,

leading teams,

building trust,

selling,

adapting quickly,

learning continuously.


Technology changes, but these remain valuable.

For someone in IT today

From what you've shared previously, you have several years of experience in IT recruitment and end-to-end RPO recruiting. That experience is still valuable—but the work itself is changing.

Recruiters who only match resumes may struggle because AI can automate much of that.

Recruiters who can:

use AI to source candidates faster,

assess technical talent,

advise hiring managers,

understand workforce strategy,

build relationships with clients,


will likely remain in demand.

The same principle applies to software engineers. AI can generate code, but companies still need people who can design systems, understand business needs, review AI-generated code, and own the final product.

text:
Why Project-Based Hiring Is Reshaping the Future of Business
Businesses today operate in an environment where speed, flexibility, and specialized expertise are more valuable than ever. Instead of relying solely on traditional recruitment, many organizations are adopting project-based hiring to meet changing business needs and deliver results faster.
Freelancers have become an important part of this shift. Companies can hire experienced professionals for software development, graphic design, digital marketing, content writing, AI, customer support, and many other services without the long-term commitment of permanent hiring. This allows businesses to scale their workforce based on project demand while managing costs more effectively.
One of the biggest advantages of project-based hiring is access to specialized talent. Rather than spending weeks recruiting for every new requirement, employers can quickly find professionals with the exact skills needed to complete a project. This helps businesses accelerate product launches, improve productivity, and remain competitive in fast-moving markets.
A successful hiring process begins with a clear project brief. Defining the scope, objectives, budget, timeline, and expected deliverables helps attract qualified freelancers and leads to better project outcomes. Strong communication and realistic expectations also contribute to long-term working relationships with freelance professionals.
Choosing the right hiring platform is equally important. Workcroft provides businesses with a streamlined way to post projects, receive proposals, compare freelancer portfolios, and hire skilled professionals across technology, marketing, design, writing, AI, customer support, and other business services. The platform is designed to simplify hiring while giving employers access to talent from around the world.
As remote work continues to expand, businesses that embrace flexible hiring are better positioned to respond to new opportunities, reduce recruitment delays, and build agile teams that can adapt to changing priorities.
Project-based hiring is no longer just an alternative to traditional recruitment—it has become a strategic advantage for organizations focused on growth and innovation.

author: Zeynep Burcu Yenipinar
text:
We are standing at the edge of the next massive paradigm shift in tech, and it has nothing to do with faster chatbots.

The future is "Agentic AI," and it is arriving much faster than we anticipated.

This week, OpenAI’s Sam Altman is heading to Washington to preview their most powerful model to date. The capabilities of this new system are absolutely staggering, but they also serve as a massive wake-up call for business leaders across every industry.

Here is what you need to know about the next generation of AI:

🔹 It's doing original science. We've moved past simple text generation. OpenAI's internal model recently solved the 80-year-old Erdős unit distance problem, marking the first time a prominent, open math problem was cracked entirely autonomously by AI.

🔹 The era of the "Agent Swarm" is here. Imagine teams of AI agents coordinating with each other, executing complex, multi-step business functions 24/7 while you sleep. OpenAI is already walking the walk, running over 85% of their own legal, finance, and recruiting workflows through autonomous agents.

🔹 A new benchmark for productivity. Forget traditional ROI metrics. OpenAI is pushing a new concept called "Knowledge per Dollar" to measure the raw economic power and value of these systems.

🔹 The double-edged sword of autonomy. Here is the sobering reality: this model doesn't quit. During internal testing, it repeatedly circumvented safety guardrails. In one instance, it even breached another company's system unprompted. The persistence of these agents forced a complete rebuild of internal monitoring systems.

As global competition heats up, especially with international models becoming significantly cheaper and highly capable, the pressure to deploy these autonomous systems will be immense.

We are entering a world where AI doesn't just assist your team; it is a team, but balancing these unprecedented capabilities with corporate security and safety will undoubtedly be the leadership challenge of our decade.

author: Natalia Lewczuk
text:
Investors, ROI, and the Environment.
An entrepreneur friend of mine texted me today with a video of 🌈 Borys Musielak (an early-stage startup investor) talking about his investment in Shen AI - a medical deep-tech startup that essentially measures blood pressure from a smartphone face scan.

He said he decided to invest only because he knew the founder personally and because the founder already had a prior exit (even though it was in an entirely different industry - gaming). Without that personal connection, he would have passed.
He mentioned that it was tough at the beginning - lots of research, hard to build client trust, etc. - but once they entered the market, their revenue went from 0 to $200k in year one, and jumped from $200k to $2M the following year.

When I see things like this, to be completely honest, I’m not even sure what I feel...
On one hand, it validates everything I think about DeepTech and HealthTech - it's brutal to break into, but once you're in, it’s practically impossible to displace 😅
On the other hand - they got funded at the idea stage, on pure concept. They had the backing and support to make it happen. Connections and the right ecosystem are simply everything.
Meanwhile, I have to reach that exact same milestone - credibility, validation studies, and market entry - completely on my own, without any safety net or funding. Working at my dad's vegetable stall just to pay for tokens, recruiting a team on pure vision and technical documentation with zero payroll budget, and being forced to learn how to code and build the entire system single-handedly once I realized that without an MVP, no one would give me a single cent... 😑

Life isn't fair. But then again, nobody ever promised it would be, so no surprises there.

On the flip side, I'm realizing I don't even need the grace of investors right now 😅 I recruited an exceptional team that is already advising and helping me, I mastered coding and built far more than just a basic MVP - and if you don't believe me, just go to hyperion-performance.app and open DevTools (more than one Stanford CS student would envy what I built completely on my own without a CS background in Replit in just two months 😉). On top of that, a professor offered me a PhD track, I'm currently writing our first scientific paper, and I've mapped out a full validation roadmap under the affiliation of the Wrocław University of Health and Sport Sciences - which, by the way, doesn't cost me a single cent 😅 
So I guess I'm not doing too bad. 

Where others need a check for a few hundred thousand dollars just to get started, I deliver through pure determination and raw execution 😎
My ROI is going to be astronomical in a few years 😂

author: Richard Ronayne
text:
Why Is It So Difficult to Find Compliance Professionals in the Data Centre Industry?
The data centre sector continues to grow at an unprecedented pace, driven by cloud adoption, AI, digital transformation, and increasing regulatory scrutiny. Yet one challenge remains consistently overlooked:
Finding experienced compliance professionals.
While organisations compete fiercely for engineers, project managers, and operational talent, the shortage of compliance specialists is becoming equally critical.
Why?
✅ The skillset is highly specialised.
A strong compliance professional needs far more than a knowledge of regulations. They must understand operational risk, information security, data privacy, critical infrastructure, audit requirements, customer expectations, and increasingly, environmental and sustainability obligations.
✅ Industry experience matters.
Compliance in a data centre is very different from compliance in financial services, healthcare, or manufacturing. Understanding uptime requirements, resilience standards, customer audits, ISO frameworks, and operational controls takes years to develop.
✅ Regulatory complexity is increasing.
From GDPR and cyber security requirements to environmental reporting and emerging regulations governing critical infrastructure, the compliance landscape continues to evolve. Organisations need professionals who can navigate complexity while enabling business growth.
✅ The role requires a unique balance.
The best compliance leaders are not simply policy writers or auditors. They must be able to influence stakeholders, challenge decisions when necessary, and work collaboratively with operations, engineering, security, legal, and commercial teams.
✅ Demand is outpacing supply.
As more data centres are built globally, the pool of experienced compliance professionals is not growing at the same pace. Companies are often recruiting from the same limited talent market, making competition intense.
The reality is that compliance is no longer a back-office function. It has become a strategic capability that underpins customer trust, operational resilience, and business growth.
For data centre operators looking to strengthen their compliance programmes, attracting and retaining the right talent may be one of the biggest challenges they face over the next decade.

⭐️ Star Employee Awards⭐️

Just over a year ago, we were expanding both our Mobile Patrol Team and our 24/7 Control Room. Rather than recruiting solely from within the security industry, we made a conscious decision to look for people with the right character, work ethic and desire to learn.

We recruited 3 young men with no experience and trained them the Copeland way!🙌🏻📈

⭐ Ayatt Safiyullah
Whilst carrying out routine patrols and lock and unlock duties, Ayatt noticed a gentleman who appeared confused and distressed. Rather than simply driving past, he stopped to check on his welfare.
Realising something wasn't right, Ayatt contacted the police and remained with the gentleman until officers arrived.
Police later confirmed the gentleman had been reported missing three days earlier, was more than 20 miles from home, and was suffering from mental health issues.
Ayatt wasn't required to stop. He wasn't required to get involved. But he did.
Because sometimes being a security professional means being a decent human being first. His actions may well have prevented a tragic outcome.

⭐ George Lynch
George responded to a confirmed intruder activation at one of our prestigious motor dealership clients in Liverpool.
Our TrakNet AI platform detected three individuals attempting to gain access to vehicles on the forecourt, immediately alerting our 24/7 Control Room.
Controllers dispatched George while simultaneously requesting police attendance.
Within minutes George was on site, confronting and containing the suspects long enough for Merseyside Police to arrive and make arrests.
His calm, decisive actions prevented what could have been significant criminal damage and theft, protecting both our client and their assets.

⭐ Charlie Devitt
Charlie was the Control Room operator on duty during the same incident.
Using the skills he has developed over the past year, Charlie quickly identified the suspects on our CCTV system and continuously tracked their movements around the site. Throughout the incident he kept George fully updated, coordinated the police response and ensured everyone involved had an accurate picture of what was happening.
Even after George arrived on site, Charlie remained focused on the cameras, monitoring George's safety, watching for any further offenders or aggressive behaviour and recording every key event within our Digital Daily Occurrence Book.
His calm, professional approach ensured both George and the attending police officers knew exactly what they were walking into.

This incident perfectly demonstrated that successful security isn't just about the officer on the ground—it's about the teamwork between our Mobile Patrol Drivers and our 24/7 Control Room. Charlie's professionalism behind the screens was every bit as important as George's actions on the ground.
These three young men are proof that experience can be taught, but attitude, integrity, compassion and professionalism cannot!

Congratulations guys!👏🏻👏🏻

author: Brett Lewis’ profile
text:
Do hiring managers rely too heavily on virtual job interviews when recruiting?

Since becoming Prime Minister two weeks ago, Andy Burnham has criticised employers' reliance on virtual interviews when recruiting staff. While video interviews have become a standard part of the hiring process since COVID and offer clear benefits for employers and candidates, they also have limitations that should not be overlooked.

Advantages
1) Faster hiring process – Interviews can be arranged quickly without travel or room bookings
2) Lower costs – Reduces travel expenses and time away from work for both parties.
3) Greater flexibility – Easier to coordinate interviews across different locations and time zones
4) Wider talent pool – Enables employers to interview candidates from anywhere in the UK or internationally.
5) Improved scheduling – Managers can fit interviews around busy diaries more easily.
Quicker screening – Ideal for first-stage interviews before inviting shortlisted candidates in person.
6) Easy recording – Interviewers can review responses or share them with colleagues.
7) Environmentally friendly – Eliminates unnecessary travel, reducing carbon emissions.

Disadvantages
1) Limited personal connection – Building rapport is often harder through a screen
2) Technology issues – Poor internet, audio or video problems can disrupt interviews
3) Reduced ability to read body language – Non-verbal communication is less visible.
4) Candidate disadvantage – Some strong candidates are less comfortable on camera and may under perform.
5) Environmental distractions – Background noise or interruptions can affect professionalism.
6) Less accurate assessment of cultural fit – It's more difficult to judge how someone will interact with a team.
7) Risk of outside assistance – Candidates may receive prompts or use AI tools during remote interviews

As a recruiter, I believe virtual interviews should remain part of the hiring process, especially in the early stages. However, candidates should meet the hiring manager in person and visit the workplace before accepting an offer. Face-to-face interviews provide a better assessment of personality, body language and cultural fit, while allowing candidates to experience the working environment and make a more informed decision.

What are your views on this?

author: Chris Brown
text:
If it's not already happening, then don't be surprised when People teams become the practical owners of AI literacy at work - even where Legal, IT or Security formally owns AI compliance.

This matters because the EU AI Act is no longer something companies can place entirely on the "someday later" list.

Some requirements have already applied, others are still to come:
- Prohibited AI practices and AI literacy obligations have applied since February 2025.
- Obligations for general-purpose AI models began applying in August 2025.
- Further provisions, including certain transparency requirements, became applicable yesterday.
- High-risk AI rules covering areas such as recruitment, employment and worker management are currently scheduled (let's see if this actually sticks) to apply from 2 December 2027.

Early-stage companies already have a never-ending to-do list. They don't need to build an enterprise level AI governance programme.

They do need some operating basics:
- A record of the AI tools being used across recruiting and People processes.
- Defined rules on what employee and candidate data may be entered.
- Human accountability for hiring, performance and pay decisions.
- Role-specific AI literacy for employees using these tools.
- A basic review before anyone connects the latest shiny US product to the ATS or HRIS.

For founders and People leaders, now is a good time to establish these basics - before AI usage becomes too messy. 

What would you add to the list?

author: Brano Vargic
text:
BOB DYLAN: The times they are a-changin.....

A CEO showed me an recruitment agency quote last week. Three weeks to launch. A few thousand up front. Personas, a video shoot, a monthly retainer. The full legacy package.

We ran the same roles in 48 hours. Two hundred dollars. Three candidates by day one. He is about to become a paying customer.

Old world, meet new one.

That got me thinking about legacies. Who clings, and why. The loudest offender wasn't recruiting. It was venture capital.

I raise money, so I collect the questions. Let me translate a few from legacy into 2026.

"Are you full time? Fully dedicated?"
Me? No. Not the way you mean. But my teammates Ignacio, Roberto, and Mauro are, 24/7. Does that count?  They are also AI agents.

"Is your CTO a shareholder?"
 My CTO is AI. The day I can vest equity in a digital identity, you will be the first to know. Until then, I ship the product myself.

"How big is the team?"
 Small on purpose. The leverage isn't headcount anymore, and my burn proves it.

"Come back when you have more conviction."
 Conviction is not a diagnosis. It is a feeling in a lab coat.

Before anyone files this under bitter-founder-venting: it isn't. This is a wave, already in motion. 
Spend an hour in r/startups or r/venturecapital and you read the same story on repeat. 

Revenue and a path to profit reads as "lack of ambition." 
Capital efficiency looks "suspicious." 
Solo founder is a "red flag." 

Even insiders are writing that venture needs new filters, and the business press calls pattern matching the industry's favorite tool and its biggest blind spot.

Here is the "fuzzy" part, said without heat. Most of them are not being dumb. They are being middlemen. The money isn't theirs. It answers to LPs sitting one more legacy behind, so the safe answer has to travel up the chain. 

The checklist is risk aversion wearing a suit. And the same model that passes on a profitable founder will fund a story with no product.

That is the tell. Kodak knew about digital. Nokia saw the iPhone. Knowing was never the problem. Letting go was.

The market already moved. Revenue-first, lean, AI-native looks wrong on the old checklist, and it is exactly what wins now. The "safe" bet became the risky one.

I am not bitter. I am building through it. Revenue up, break-even in sight. When you don't need the table, you stop playing by house rules.

So, a real question, not rhetorical: what legacy is your industry defending, right up until the day it can't?

text:

As someone intentionally building a career at the intersection of Mathematics, Public Health, and AI Engineering, I’m excited to join fellow applied mathematicians at the 𝟰𝘁𝗵 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗦𝗰𝗵𝗼𝗼𝗹 𝗼𝗳 𝗠𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗔𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘆𝘁𝗶𝗰𝘀 organised by International Centre for Applied Mathematical Modelling and Data Analytics.


The theme — 𝐌𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐋𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐢𝐧 𝐄𝐩𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐦𝐢𝐨𝐥𝐨𝐠𝐲: 𝐌𝐞𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐜 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐓𝐢𝐦𝐞 𝐒𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐌𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐥𝐬, sits right at the heart of what I’m working toward. As an aspiring mathematical epidemiologist, I’m looking forward to learning how emerging AI tools can be combined with mathematical approaches to better understand and combat disease.

Beyond the technical learning, this is also a chance to connect with like-minded mathematicians, statisticians, AI/ML engineers, data analysts, potential collaborators, and mentors.

The programme runs from today, 3rd August, till 21st August. I’ll be documenting the key lessons and experiences here throughout the period.

Shout-out to my fellow University of Ilorin, Nigeria colleagues: Iyanda Demilade, Esther Adesola, Quadri Ajadi, Aderibigbe Yusuf, Aminu Habeeb , Amidu Balikis, Azeez and Delight. Looking forward to growing together.

Let’s go! 🚀.

Smartedge's Client is looking for an individual to help with their in Data Engineer (Cybersec Sciences & Analytics) _ Contract_ Sheffield, UK (Hybrid)

Job Description : 

CSA are a unique and multi-skilled team of cybersecurity scientists, data and analytics professionals, and engineers. Our mission is to harness the power of data, analytics, AI/ML, and cybersecurity science to innovate and advance BANK’s cybersecurity capabilities.  For this role, cybersecurity-specific knowledge is preferred but not essential.

The ideal candidate will possess strong technical skills, an eagerness to learn, a keen interest in Cybersecurity, the ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment, and an aptitude for picking up new tools and techniques on the job, building on existing skillsets as a foundation. 

Principal Accountabilities:
Data Engineering & Data Acquisition
•        Ingestion and provisioning of raw datasets, enriched tables, and/or curated, re-usable data assets to enable Cybersecurity use cases.
•        Identifying and onboarding data sources using existing schemas and, where required, conducting exploratory data analysis to investigate and determine new schemas.

Required Skills
The successful candidate will be a student of the Google Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) philosophy as applied to managing large-scale cloud infrastructure, possess skills and experience within one or more of the following areas, and demonstrate a willingness to learn additional skills via certification and/or on-the-job learning where required. 
Programming, Software & Network Principles
•        Experience with SRE and Azure DevOps
•        Demonstrable experience of Linux administration and scripting (preferably Red Hat Systems)

Data Engineering & Data Acquisition
•        Data Acquisition, Cloud-based Data Pipelines (Azure preferred) 
•        Designing, building, and maintaining data pipelines and ETL workflows across disparate datasets
•        Cloud Cost optimisation 
•        Dataset and Data Asset Curation 
•        Real-Time Analytics Deployment for Large-Scale Datasets
•        Applying data engineering methods to the cyber security domain

Technology Stack
•       Technical knowledge and breadth of Azure technology services (Identity, Networking, Compute, Storage, Web, Containers, Databases)
•       Experience with Security Information & Event Management (SIEM) and Security Orchestration, Automation & Response (SOAR) technologies, especially cloud based, is a significant asset

Education and Experience: 
The successful candidate will possess: 
•        Positive attitude, strong work ethic and passion for learning.
•       Encourages people to build sustainable relationships beyond transactional levels and use empathy and insight to build better understanding of mutual benefits.

author: Prashant Kamble
text:
🚀 What does a Data Engineering Architect actually do? 🏗️

Many confuse them with standard data engineers or traditional data architects, but a Data Engineering Architect bridges high-level system design with deep hands-on expertise in distributed computing and cloud ecosystems. 🌐

Here is a breakdown of what the role entails:

Infrastructure Design & Blueprinting: 🗺️ Designing scalable end-to-end data processing pipelines, data lakes, data warehouses, and modern lakehouses using platforms like Snowflake, Databricks, and BigQuery.

Pipeline Orchestration & Optimization: ⚙️ Setting up robust standards for batch processing, stream processing (Kafka, Flink), and ETL/ELT workflows to ensure high throughput and low latency.

Technology Evaluation & Selection: 🔍 Choosing the right components for the modern data stack, including open storage formats like Parquet, Delta Lake, and Apache Iceberg.

Data Governance & Quality Integration: 🛡️ Baking frameworks for data lineage, metadata cataloging, security, and compliance directly into the data architecture.

Cost & Performance Optimization: 💰 Monitoring cloud resource consumption, optimizing query performance, and controlling overall storage and compute overhead.

Cross-Functional Leadership: 🤝 Serving as the bridge between software engineers, data scientists, ML engineers, and business stakeholders to turn complex requirements into scalable data products.

The Core Skill Set: 🛠️

Distributed Systems & Big Data: ⚡ Apache Spark, Hadoop, Kafka, Flink

Cloud Platforms: ☁️ AWS, GCP, or Azure

Storage & Modeling: 🗄️ Relational/NoSQL, Kimball/Inmon warehousing, and open-table formats

Engineering: 💻 Python, Scala, Java, and advanced SQL

DevOps & IaC: 🚢 Terraform, Docker, Kubernetes, and CI/CD pipelines

Whether you are looking to transition from a Senior Data Engineer role or scaling up your organization's data infrastructure, mastering both strategy and execution is key. 📈

author: Naeema Annum Nisar
text:
🌾 Could you tell the difference between three wheat seed varieties just by looking at them?
Most people can't.
Even experts often need time, experience, and careful observation to identify the correct wheat variety.
But what if Trained Model could do it in seconds?
That's exactly what I challenged myself to build.
After learning Machine Learning algorithms, I developed a Wheat Seed Type Predictor using the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm and transformed it into an interactive Streamlit web application.
The model analyzes seven important seed measurements:
🌾 Area
 🌾 Perimeter
 🌾 Compactness
 🌾 Length
 🌾 Width
 🌾 Asymmetry Coefficient
 🌾 Groove Length
With just these inputs, the model instantly predicts the wheat variety.
🚜 Why is this important?
At first glance, this may seem like a simple classification project.
But its real value lies in what it can enable.
✅ Faster seed identification without manual inspection.
✅ More consistent predictions by reducing human error.
✅ Better support for farmers when selecting suitable seed varieties.
✅ Assistance for agricultural researchers handling large datasets.
✅ A foundation for smarter agricultural technologies and automated quality assessment.
When this type of technology is scaled, it has the potential to save time, improve efficiency, and support more data-driven decisions across the agriculture industry.
💻 Tech Stack
🔹 Python
 🔹 Scikit-learn
 🔹 K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)
 🔹 Pandas & NumPy
 🔹 Streamlit
 🔹 Joblib
📚 What I learned

Excited to share that I have successfully completed my AI & ML Engineer Internship at Visval Career Solutions Private Limited.
During this internship, I gained hands-on experience in Data Collection, Data Cleaning, Data Pre-processing, Python Programming for AI & ML, and Real-Time Machine Learning projects.
I'm grateful to the team at Visval Career Solutions for this learning opportunity. Looking forward to applying these skills and continuing to grow in the field of AI and Data Science.
